passage:
The school library tested a face scanner to make borrowing books faster. Students only had to stand in front of a screen, and their names appeared.
Some students thought it was convenient. Others felt uncomfortable. They asked where the face data would be stored, who could see it, and whether students could refuse.
The librarian paused the test and held a meeting. After listening to students, the library returned to using cards and added a faster barcode system instead.
The scanner was advanced, but the school decided speed was not the only value.
Technology should answer more than "Can we do this?" It should also answer "Should we do this here, and who might be affected?"
